parcalar.metin: [gerilim] Five days... three massive crashes! In America, first email went down, then the planes, then the banks.
[anlatici] November 12. Microsoft's Outlook, Teams and Copilot crashed worldwide.
[vurgu] The cause: a technical failure, the company says, not a cyberattack. The result: businesses and government offices were disrupted for two days.
[gerilim] November 13. With thirty-five hundred planes in the air, controllers suddenly couldn't hear their pilots.
[anlatici] The cause: a new router, installed in Arkansas during a copper-to-fiber upgrade, flooded the network with a thousand log-on attempts every four to five seconds.
[vurgu] The result: seventeen of twenty-two centers were hit, every departure stopped, and over twelve thousand flights were canceled that day.
[anlatici] November 16. This time, the banks. Chase got close to twenty thousand outage reports.
[vurgu] The cause: a technical glitch, the bank says. The result: logins, balances and Zelle transfers froze, and the problem reached the branches.
[soru] So, was it an attack? All three said no. And no link between them was found.
[vurgu] The common lesson: these systems hang on a single point, and they break most when they're being upgraded. The Transportation Secretary asked Congress for fifty billion dollars.
[vurgu] The wires are getting replaced... but one single box can still stop a country. Follow Black Box Files for the next case.
